key_insight: A flow-based generative model can learn a physically meaningful probability distribution of turbulent channel flow that supports both synthetic turbulence generation and conditional flow reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: This enables more realistic turbulence initial conditions and sparse-observation reconstruction for CFD, potentially reducing dependence on expensive direct numerical simulation data.
method: Train a flow-based generative model on a minimal conditional flow unit from channel-flow DNS at Re_tau=180.
Use a consistent conditional sampling procedure to generate fields given a single center observation.
Evaluate physical ensemble statistics, conditional-sampling consistency, and dynamical invariance against DNS.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that generated fields reproduce key turbulence statistics and dynamics, and when used as DNS initial conditions they remain physical and statistically stationary.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated for channel flow at Re_tau=180, so transferability to higher Reynolds numbers or other geometries may require retraining and careful validation.
paper_title: A machine-learned probability distribution in the phase space of turbulent channel flow for synthetic turbulence and flow reconstruction
